name: [GFF99] C08
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy M91 that pulsates every 38.2 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 38.19 d in Kanbur et al. (2003), A&A 411, 361, VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC4548, Cepheid = C8 (log(P) 1.582); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 38.19 d in Kanbur et al. (2003), A&A 411, 361, VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC4548, Cepheid = C8 (log(P) 1.582); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M91, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261...21Y; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M91 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 16,187,457 pc (src/objects/m91-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 16,188,254 pc, inclination 38.3 deg, line of nodes 138 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully et al. (2023), Cosmicflows-4, ApJ 944, 94; CDS J/ApJ/944/94, table 2 (distances of individual galaxies), PGC 41934: distance modulus 31.046 ± 0.048 mag (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJ/944/94)

position.credit: Kanbur et al. (2003), A&A 411, 361, VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC4548, Cepheid = C8, names the star in SIMBAD (SName); SIMBAD holds its position, from 1999ApJ...516..626G

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy M91, 16.2 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 38.2 days.
text.introduction: Kanbur et al. (2003) list its pulsation at 38.2 days.
text.locator: VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC4548, Cepheid = C8: log(P)

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M91 is not measured
